image_description: A close-up, low-angle shot of a vertical traffic light suspended from overhead wires against a clear blue sky. The traffic light housing is dark gray/black with three circular lenses stacked vertically: red (top, illuminated), amber/yellow (middle, unlit but visible), and green (bottom, illuminated). Each lens has a textured, faceted surface typical of LED or prismatic lenses. Visors (hoods) extend over each lens. To the left of the main signal head is a cylindrical backplate or mounting structure. Overhead utility wires are visible at the top.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'green' lens texture; AI often generates uniform grids instead of complex prismatic patterns. Also, scrutinize the top mounting area—AI frequently fails to render rigid mechanical clamps for suspended objects, resulting in 'floating' or 'melted' wire connections. Verify if the red and green lights being simultaneously on is a physical possibility (usually indicates a malfunction or specific arrow signal, but here they are full circles, which is a potential logical error in real-world physics, though not necessarily an image generation artifact).
